web_blocks.title: Technical & Volatility Rule: Respect the Correction Regime
paragraphs: TXN's Stage 2 chart stays healthy, but 6 market distribution days warn against chasing $303.60 (1.00:1 vs 2.46:1 at support). Let price come to the $278–$286 shelf, or use the Sept 2027 $280 LEAPS Call only after support holds.

book_paragraphs: From a technical and institutional-flow perspective, Texas Instruments sits in a textbook Weinstein Stage 2 uptrend, but it is currently caught between a strong individual chart and a fragile broader market. As of November 13, 2026, TXN closed at $303.60, down 2.84% on the day, yet up 7.36% over one week and 7.04% over one month on TradingView (+9.46% 1W and +8.77% 1M in the [S9.1] Finviz snapshot window), +10.96% over three months, and +86.80% over one year. At $303.60, TXN trades +6.95% above its 50-day SMA ($283.87) and +6.12% above its 30-week SMA ($286.10), just 9.11% below its $334.03 52-week high.

Every key trendline is stacked in bullish order beneath the price. On the daily chart, the 10-day SMA sits at $300.37, the 20-day at $296.85, the 50-day at $283.87, and the 200-day at $264.77. On the weekly chart, the 10-week EMA is $285.85, the 30-week SMA is $286.10, and the 40-week EMA is $264.24. Momentum oscillators confirm healthy digestion: 14-day RSI is 54.83, 14-week RSI is 58.69, and 4-hour RSI is 52.54. Friday's 2.84% dip came on light volume of 5.23 million shares—0.65x TradingView's 7.99 million 30-day average (or 0.77x Finviz's 6.78 million average)—showing no institutional dumping. Institutions own 91.92% of the float (+2.16% QoQ), and short interest is 2.01%.

So why not buy immediately at $303.60? Two reasons: market regime and reward-to-risk math. First, the broader US market is in a Correction regime—below its 50-day moving average, with only 52.6% of stocks above their 50-DMA, 47.4% above their 200-DMA, and 6 distribution days logged in the past 25 sessions across SPY ($754.37), QQQ ($679.89), and SOXX ($149.30). Meanwhile, rising Treasury yields tighten risk appetite: US10Y sits at 5.10% (+20 bps WoW) and US2Y sits at 4.86% (+28 bps WoW). In a rate-pressured Correction, Stage 2 leaders routinely pull back to test their 10-week and 50-day moving averages.

Second, buying at $303.60 puts your structural stop-loss—at $262.00, just below the 200-day SMA ($264.77) and 40-week EMA ($264.24)—$41.60 below entry, while our $345.00 base target sits $41.40 above entry. That is a flat 1.00-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio, far below our 1.50-to-1 minimum threshold. By contrast, waiting patiently for a pullback into the $278.00 to $286.00 institutional shelf—where the S1 pivot ($277.54), 50-day SMA ($283.87), 10-week EMA ($285.85), and 30-week SMA ($286.10) converge—cuts risk to $24.00 per share against $59.00 of base-case upside, lifting asymmetry to 2.46-to-1.

book_subsections.title: Options Convexity: Why the Sept 2027 LEAPS Call Is Cheap
paragraphs: For investors who want defined-risk upside exposure without committing $30,360 for 100 shares, the options market offers an unusually attractive volatility setup. TXN's at-the-money implied volatility sits at 49.6%, well below its 20-day realized historical volatility of 57.1%—an IV-cheap regime where option sellers are not charging panic premiums.

Our Options Desk highlights the September 17, 2027 $280 LEAPS Call (306 days to expiration, 0.69 delta) priced near $64.53 per share, or $6,453.00 per contract. That single contract behaves like roughly 69 shares of TXN ($68.70 of P&L per $1 stock move) while losing only $9.81 per day to time decay and strictly capping maximum possible loss at $6,453.00. Breakeven at expiration is $344.53 (+13.48% from CMP). More importantly, pairing the LEAPS with an early exit rule on a weekly close below $286.10 caps modeled downside to roughly -$961.79 (-14.9%), while a move to $349.14 (+15.0% in the stock) generates a +36.3% option return and $401.51 (+32.2%) delivers +106.5%.

Always keep liquidity and execution discipline in mind when trading long-dated options. The September 2027 $280 Call currently carries a $63.05 bid and $66.00 ask on 50 contracts of open interest, so traders should never place market orders—always work limit orders near the $64.53 mid-price. Crucially, because TXN at $303.60 sits +6.95% above its 50D SMA ($283.87) and +6.12% above its 30W SMA ($286.10), this options_snapshot.py LEAPS Call ($6,453 max loss, $344.53 breakeven) is gated strictly on a pullback to $278.00–$286.00 and scaled to No-FOMO risk units—NOT an immediate entry at $303.60 CMP.

Finally, let us note the sector backdrop. TheWrap ranks Semiconductors at #12 overall, with 100% of tracked semiconductor names outperforming the S&P 500. Yet within analog semis, performance has diverged sharply: TXN (+86.80% 1Y) and ADI (+66.07% 1Y) are leading in Stage 2 above their 50-day and 200-day moving averages, while MCHP ($61.68 vs SMA50 $73.73), ON ($71.06 vs SMA50 $74.06), and STM ($46.73 vs SMA50 $49.31) remain stuck below their 50-day and 200-day averages. Institutional capital is clearly crowding into Tier-1 quality—giving us even more confidence that TXN's $278–$286 shelf will attract buyers on a market-driven pullback.

To summarize the tape discipline: respect the six distribution days on the major indices, refuse to chase $303.60 when the 10-week EMA ($285.85) and 30-week SMA ($286.10) sit 6% below, and let price come to the $278.00–$286.00 institutional shelf. Whether you express that entry in common shares or in the IV-cheap September 2027 $280 LEAPS Call, waiting for support turns a mediocre 1.00:1 trade into an institutional-grade 2.46:1 setup.

Think about the psychology of a Correction regime for a moment. When SPY ($754.37) and QQQ ($679.89) log six distribution days in twenty-five sessions and fewer than half of tracked stocks remain above their 200-day moving averages (47.4%), institutional portfolio managers tighten risk budgets and wait to deploy cash at major weekly moving averages. They do not chase +7.36% one-week bounces on 0.65x volume. By placing your bid at the $278.00–$286.00 institutional shelf and anchoring your stop at $262.00—right below the 200-day SMA ($264.77) and 40-week EMA ($264.24)—you align your capital with the exact price zone where long-only funds defend Stage 2 leadership.

Notice also how cleanly the execution rules fit together. Set alerts at $286.10 (the 30-week simple moving average) and $278.00 (just above the S1 pivot at $277.54). When TXN pulls into that band and prints a reversal bar on expanding volume—or when the broader market stops printing distribution days—you can step in knowing your downside to the $262.00 hard stop is strictly bounded at 8.4% while your upside to $345.00 is 20.6%.

Conversely, what if TXN never pulls back to $286.00 and instead breaks out above R1 ($318.60) and the 52-week high ($334.03) on heavy institutional volume? If the broad market simultaneously exits Correction via a confirmed Follow-Through Day, our existing 1.6917 Schwab shares participate directly in that upside, and we can trail our hard stop upward behind rising weekly moving averages without ever having chased an extended entry.
